findings.summary: API fixture leaves titles random (setup_bookmark default), so title order is not controlled and a wrong sort mapping could pass by chance
findings.failure_scenario: Suppose an implementation wrongly maps modified_asc to order_by('title'). The three titles come from get_random_string, so 1 run in 6 sorts them as b, c, a. When that happens, test_list_bookmarks_sort_modified_asc passes even though the code is broken. Giving the bookmarks fixed titles whose order differs from every expected order (as the e2e fixture does with Alpha/Bravo/Charlie) removes the chance.

findings.summary: The unknown-sort fallback test also passes on the code before the change, which the strategy says every test must not do
findings.failure_scenario: On base 0837b51, ?sort=bogus already falls back to -date_added, so this test is green both before and after the change. That is expected for a 'still falls back' regression criterion, but it should be labelled as a regression guard and not counted as evidence that the feature works. Its fixture does separate the default order from added_asc and both modified orders, so a fallback that silently switched to one of those would be caught.
